title: Weather Forces Surya Kiran Team to Cut Short Mysuru Dasara Air Display
excerpt: Low cloud over the Bannimantap Grounds forced the nine-jet Surya Kiran team back to Yelahanka on Sunday; a full display, including a Mysuru Palace flyby, is planned for Monday if the weather clears.
body:
• The Indian Air Force's Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team could not fly its full display over Mysuru on Sunday, October 18, after adverse weather forced the nine Hawk Mk 132 jets to return to Air Force Station Yelahanka.
  • Team officers said a low cloud base and obstructions around the Bannimantap Grounds, including Chamundi Hills about 5 km away, made the close-formation profile unsafe.
  • The team plans to attempt its full display, including loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the signature DNA manoeuvre, on Monday, October 19, subject to favourable weather.
  • Visitors in Mysuru for Dasara can check the day's programme on the official Mysuru Dasara events page before heading to Bannimantap.

The Indian Air Force's Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team was unable to showcase its full air display over Mysuru on Sunday after adverse weather conditions intervened, The Hindu reported. The nine-aircraft team, scheduled to perform over the Bannimantap Grounds on October 18 and 19 as part of the city's Dasara festivities, took off from Air Force Station Yelahanka but had to return to base without completing its display profile.

"Due to prevailing weather conditions, the team could not undertake its complete display profile," the team said in a statement. Group Captain Ajay Dasarathi, the team's commanding officer, took the call to abandon the full display.

Why the weather mattered

Aerobatic display flying leaves little margin for poor visibility. Squadron Leader Tushar Sharma explained that a nine-aircraft formation needs a minimum cloud base because the jets cannot descend too close to the ground, and the terrain around the venue adds to the constraint. "There are few obstructions around the Bannimantap Grounds, including the Chamundi Hills, which is about 5 km from the ground. Due to the prevailing weather conditions we decided to return to the base," he said.

"There are certain synchro maneuvers which we perform wherein some of the members will split and two members cross in front of each other with a distance of less than five meters at a speed of close to 1,000 kmph."

— Squadron Leader Tushar Sharma, Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team

Sharma said spectators who stay on for Monday's attempt can expect the team's signature manoeuvres, including loops, barrel rolls and inverted flying, along with the DNA manoeuvre. Two aircraft will also draw a heart in the sky, he said, as a gesture to the people of Mysuru.

A special profile for Dasara

For this year's festivities, the team has prepared a display profile specific to Mysuru. "If weather permits, we have a flyby where we will try to depict the shape of the Mysuru palace in the air which is a special dedication to the people of Mysuru," Sharma said. The air show was arranged after Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar requested Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to include the aerobatic display in the festival, a move intended in part to encourage local youth to consider careers in the armed forces, according to India Strategic's preview of the show. Military tableaux representing the Army, Navy and Air Force also feature in this year's Dasara procession.

The Surya Kiran team, established in 1996, flies the Hawk Mk 132 and has recently introduced new formations. Squadron Leader Lalith Verma said the new formations — named Tejas, Sukhoi and Rafale — are dedicated to the Air Force's newer aircraft inventory, alongside formations named Gaganyaan, BrahMos and Akash.

What happens next

The team's remaining Mysuru slot is Monday, October 19, and whether the full profile flies depends on the cloud base over Bannimantap on the morning of the show. The wider Dasara programme continues regardless: the festival, which opened on Chamundi Hill on October 11, runs through Vijayadashami on October 21, when the Jamboo Savari procession carries the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari from the palace to Bannimantap. For diaspora families following the festival from abroad, Monday's display is the last scheduled chance to see the nine-jet formation over the city this Dasara — weather permitting.
